To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
κ-casein contains two types of chymotryptic polypeptide, and the longer type is a C-terminal fragment comprising residues 94-169.

(i) κ-casein is cleaved by rennet in the presence of calcium ions at a specific bond in the C-terminal region of the molecule, (ii) the chymosins are the active enzymes, (iii) a variant of κ-casein exists in milk, (iv) the variant is cleaved at the same site as the main form, (v) the variant is present in the same proportions in all milks, (vi) the variant differs from κ-case
the chymosinsensitive polypeptide from κ-casein is not identical with κ-casein and that the chymotryptic cleavage of κcasein at pH 3 is not a specific one.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a detailed study of the properties of the chymotrypsin-sensitive bond in κ-caseins from a number of species.
the structure of bovine κ-casein and its interaction with chymosin, and the data presented are discussed in relation to this.
the properties of a chymosin-resistant peptide of bovine κ-casein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
κ-casein contains at least two distinct regions of high chymosin sensitivity.
the amino acid sequence of κ-casein is variable, that there are at least three variants of the protein, and that these variants have different chymosin sensitivities.
the chymosinalpha s1 -casein bond is cleaved in κ-casein by the same mechanism as in the α s1 -caseins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chymosinic cleavage of κ casein at pH 3 and 6·7 occurs at the same bond, but in different conformations of the protein.
chymosin cleaves the peptide bond in the C-terminal region of κ-casein and that the sensitivity of this bond is determined by the structure of residues 94–167 in the protein.
κ-casein is not a single protein but a group of related molecules with a number of variants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amino acid sequence of a protein can be used to predict its sensitivity to proteolysis.
the chymosinsensitive polypeptide and C-terminal segment of κ-caseins are similar in amino acid composition, and that this is consistent with a specific cleavage at a single site on the protein.
the amino acid composition of the C-terminal segments of the two polypeptides is very similar to that of the corresponding section in κ-casein, but the N-terminal sections are not.
